title.rendered: One Thing You Lack: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: “Jesus, looking at him, loved him, and said, ‘You lack one thing.'” A morning devotional on the one thing that stands between us and following Jesus fully.

content.rendered:
“Good Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?” It is a good question. From a good man. Wealthy, moral, respectful, sincere. And Jesus, in one sentence, exposed the one thing that stood between him and the Kingdom.

The Gospel For Today | Sunday, September 13, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Then Jesus, looking at him, loved him, and said to him, ‘One thing you lack: Go your way, sell whatever you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, take up the cross, and follow Me.'”
Mark 10:21 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

He ran up to Jesus and knelt in front of Him. Matthew tells us he was young. Luke tells us he was a ruler. Mark tells us he was very rich. All three tell us he asked a good question, sincerely. “Good Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?” He was not testing Jesus, as some of the Pharisees did. He was not trying to trap Him. He wanted to know. And Jesus, before answering, went through the second half of the Ten Commandments with him. “You know the commandments. Do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not bear false witness, do not defraud, honour your father and your mother.” The young ruler answered with what may have been the honest truth as he saw it. “Teacher, all these things I have kept from my youth.”

Then Mark records one of the most tender sentences in the whole New Testament. “Then Jesus, looking at him, loved him.” Jesus was not angry with the young man. He was not condescending. He was not preparing to shame him. He looked at him with love. And in love, He named the one thing that stood between the young man and the Kingdom of God. “One thing you lack: Go your way, sell whatever you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, take up the cross, and follow Me.”

The one thing was not a commandment the young ruler had broken. The one thing was the rival lord in his heart. His wealth. His portfolio. His comfort. The lifestyle he had built. Jesus was not saying that every follower must literally sell everything and give it to the poor. Jesus was saying that this particular follower must, because for him wealth had become the rival throne, and no rival throne can coexist with the throne of Christ in a human heart. The young ruler heard the answer. Mark tells us what happened next in a sentence that has echoed through two thousand years of Christian preaching. “But he was sad at this word, and went away sorrowful, for he had great possessions.”

The Passion Translation opens up the moment beautifully: “Jesus gazed upon him, and he loved what he saw. He said to him, ‘You lack one important thing. Go, sell all that you own and give it to the poor and you will have great treasure in heaven. Then come and follow me'” (Mark 10:21 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “And Jesus, looking upon him, loved him, and He said to him, You lack one thing; go and sell all you have and give [the money] to the poor, and you will have [rich] treasure in heaven; and come [and] be My disciple, [side with My party and] accompany Me” (Mark 10:21 AMPC). Side with My party. Accompany Me. Jesus was not offering a religious tune-up. He was offering an entire life-change of allegiance.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, this is one of the most searching questions the Bible ever asks any of us. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, what is your one thing? What is the rival throne in your heart that has quietly been sharing the seat with Christ? For some it is wealth, as it was for the young ruler. For others it is a relationship, a career, a reputation, a habit, an ambition, a fear. Jesus is looking at you today the way He looked at the young man in Mark 10. In love. Not to shame. But to name. And to invite. Whatever the one thing is, He is worth more than it. Do not go away sorrowful. Come and follow.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that Jesus looks at me in love and calls me to full-hearted discipleship. He is worth more than every rival throne in my heart. Today I ask You to name the one thing that has been sharing the seat with Christ. Whatever it is. Wealth. Reputation. Comfort. Ambition. Fear. I lay it down at the feet of Jesus. I refuse to go away sorrowful. I follow. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

Jesus is worth more than every rival throne in my heart. I lay down the one thing that has been sharing the seat with Him. I follow Him today, single-hearted and free.
